_comment: Suitability and ROI assessment for this project (Meta Agent OS operating on itself), recorded per the v0.6.1 Suitability And ROI Gate. Mirrors the Anti-Agent Gate and Agent Suitability Assessment already recorded in ORACLE_DIAGNOSIS.md's Schema Alignment Addendum.
workflow: Operating the Meta Agent OS staged methodology with an agentic coding tool (this repository's own self-run)

requires_judgement.reason: Diagnosis, architecture trade-offs, and risk review require weighing ambiguous repository evidence. No decision table produces an Oracle diagnosis or an Architect design.

unstructured_inputs.reason: Inputs are arbitrary repositories: unknown languages, layouts, docs, and conventions.

imperfect_answer_useful.reason: A draft diagnosis or design that a human edits is more useful than no diagnosis or design. Every output is explicitly reviewable.

human_can_recover.reason: Every output is Markdown in version control, reviewed before it drives a decision, and revertible.

justifications.judgement_required: Diagnosis and architecture trade-offs cannot be reduced to rules.
justifications.input_variability: Arbitrary repositories with no controlled schema.
justifications.tolerance_for_error: Every output is a reviewable draft; nothing executes automatically.
justifications.recoverability: Markdown in version control, human-gated, trivially revertible.
justifications.volume: A full run is occasional, not continuous. This is the weakest dimension.
justifications.stability: The method is stable; the target repositories are not.

band: Well suited (21/24). No critical dimension scores zero.

roi.reason: This project's baseline is a counterfactual (designing a multi-agent system ad hoc, without staged diagnosis), not a metered process, so scripts/roi-calculator.py cannot be run against it in the same way as a workflow with a real measured baseline. Workflows designed using this framework can and should use the calculator. Verdict recorded here as a stated judgement, not a calculation, per QS_COSTS_AND_OPTIONS.md section 19.
